target_customer: US state, local and federal government procurement teams
problem: Government procurement staff are overloaded drafting requirements, solicitations and evaluations by hand.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to government agencies, also via Carahsoft reseller

founders.name: August Chen
technical: Harvard, mechanical engineering and computer science, class of 2020

founders.name: Elton Lossner
founders.background_notes: About five years at BCG, project leader, on aerospace, defense and public sector cases.

technical_complexity.rationale: LLM document generation and evaluation with compliance requirements, plus government security needs.

defensibility.rationale: Government contracts, templates and compliance work create stickiness, but model features are copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found in sources.

market_need_then: Founders cite roughly 30 percent of procurement roles unfilled and $2.7 trillion of annual public procurement, both unverified company claims.

brand_strength.rationale: Common first name used by many companies, and no brand evidence found.

pivots.from: AI marketplace helping businesses respond to government RFPs
pivots.to: AI procurement software sold to government agencies
pivots.why: Shift to selling directly to agencies per YC launch posts

outcome_analysis: Hazel pivoted from a marketplace for government bidders to selling AI procurement software directly to agencies, and won the City of Dallas in July 2025 plus a Carahsoft listing. Funding is not verified beyond small pre-seed reports, so the stage is early, and the outcome is still open given government sales cycles.
notes: Unverified funding: about $500K pre-seed (YC, Rebel Fund, Tusk Ventures, Phoenix) from aggregators, and $125K to $130K seed in Dealroom and Yespress; not recorded as rounds. CB Insights financials describe a different Hazel. No dated competitor sources near Jan 2024 found; aggregator competitor lists look unreliable.
